q: What is the minimum public corridor width of a medical facility for overseas workers and seafarers?
n: 1.50 m; wider if waiting is placed along the corridor. Remember this: the OFW clinic "20-10-6": lab work area 20 sq. m., X-ray room 10 sq. m. (2.50 × 4.00 m), eye test distance 6 m (20 ft). Corridors 1.50 m, doors 0.86 m, exam rooms 7.43 sq. m.

q: What is the minimum floor area of the clinical working area of the MFOWS laboratory?
n: Secondary general clinical lab with HIV-testing capability: work area min. 20 m².

What testing distance must the optical room accommodate for a standard Snellen chart?
n: If the room is too short, an approved mirror system may simulate the distance.

q: What is the minimum floor area of each physical examination room?
n: Exclusive of vestibules, toilets and closets; separate rooms for male and female.

q: What area per applicant is required inside the psychological testing room?
n: Plus 4.00 m² for the psychologist's room and 1.00 m² per psychometrician.

q: What recommended illumination applies to an MFOWS examination room?
ref: DOH AO 2016-0042, Annex G (Rev. 00, 12/14/2016), item 4.7 (illumination table)
n: Exam room 500 lux; treatment and waiting-reading 300 lux; corridor 200 lux.

q: Which MFOWS room must be soundproof with double-glazed windows, insulated walls and vibration-proof flooring?
